notes.label: 2026 Budget
notes.text:
Approved by Maya Okafor on 15 December 2025. Reviewed quarterly (see Quarterly Review Q2 2026).

Revenue target: $1,050,000
Stream  ·  Target  ·  Share
Café (drinks, food, retail bags in store)  ·  $740,000  ·  70%
Wholesale  ·  $190,000  ·  18%
Online store & Subscription Service  ·  $120,000  ·  12%

Cost targets
• COGS: 34% of revenue. Green coffee, milk, pastries, packaging.
• Labor: 31%, including payroll taxes. 11 staff (4 FT baristas, 3 PT, head roaster, café manager, wholesale lead, owner draw budgeted separately).
• Rent: $4,800/month for café and roastery (lease runs to 2029).
• Equipment Loan repayments: $1,690/month.
• Marketing: 3% of revenue (~$31,500). Covers Instagram Strategy boosting, the Loyalty Program (the free drinks count here) and events.
• Repairs & maintenance: $9,000, which includes quarterly espresso servicing.
• Target net profit: 7% (~$73,500).

Assumptions that have already moved
• Green coffee was budgeted at +8% but is running at +18% (see Green Coffee Sourcing).
• Milk was budgeted flat but is up 9%.
• These are why COGS ran at 36.5% in Q2 and why we did the Pricing Review.

Not in the 2026 budget
• The Colombia origin trip (February 2027, ~$4,800).
• POS-linked inventory software.
• Compostable bags for everything (+$3,800/year). This will need a decision for the 2027 budget.

notes.label: Equipment Loan
notes.text:
Term loan from Port Alder Credit Union used to buy the 15 kg drum roaster and afterburner in March 2024.

Terms
• Principal: $85,000
• Rate: 7.2% fixed
• Term: 60 months (March 2024 to February 2029)
• Payment: $1,690/month, auto-debited on the 3rd
• Balance at the end of September 2026: about $46,300
• Secured on the roaster itself, plus a personal guarantee from Maya Okafor

Covenants
• Debt service coverage ratio of at least 1.25×, tested annually on the December year-end accounts. It was 1.62× for 2025.
• Quarterly management accounts go to the credit union within 45 days of quarter-end. Q3 is due by 14 November.

What it bought
• 15 kg roaster (~$68,000 installed). It replaced the old 5 kg machine and made wholesale growth possible (see Roasting Schedule). We're currently at about 55% of its capacity.
• Afterburner and ducting (~$14,000). This is required by the county for the roastery permit.
• Installation and electrical work (~$3,000).

Options being considered
• Refinancing: the credit union has hinted at 6.4% if we move the business checking account over. That saves about $950 over the remaining term. Probably not worth the hassle.
• Extra principal payments in December if the holiday season is strong. There's no prepayment penalty.

The $25,000 line of credit mentioned in Cash Flow Q3 2026 is a separate facility with the same lender. See also 2026 Budget.

notes.label: Pricing Review
notes.text:
Decision made 18 August 2026 after Q2 margins came in 2.5 points under budget (see Quarterly Review Q2 2026). Takes effect 1 October 2026.

Why
• Green coffee is up 18% year-on-year (see Green Coffee Sourcing).
• Milk is up 9%, and oat milk is up 6%.
• The state minimum wage rises in January 2027, and our starting pay needs to stay ahead of it (see Staff Handbook).
• We haven't raised café prices since March 2024.

Drip coffee (12 oz)  ·  $3.50  ·  $3.75

12 oz retail bag, Harbor Dark  ·  $18.00  ·  $19.50
12 oz single origin  ·  $21.00  ·  $22.50
Wholesale  ·  see Wholesale Pricing  ·  about +6% across tiers

• Subscriptions: existing subscribers keep their current price until 1 January 2027, then +$1.00 per shipment. New subscribers pay the new price immediately (see Subscription Service).

Expected impact
• About +$36,000/year in gross profit if volume holds.
• We assume a 2–3% drop in café transactions for about 6 weeks. We'll watch Loyalty Program visit frequency as an early warning.

Communication
• A small counter sign from 24 September: "Coffee costs are up, so our prices are too. Here's why." A short, honest explanation in our voice per the Brand Guidelines.
• Wholesale accounts got letters from Tom Whitaker on 1 September (30 days' notice).

notes.label: Brand Guidelines
notes.text:
Short version of the brand book (v2.1, refreshed in January 2026).

Name & logo
• Always "Harbor Lane Coffee Roasters" in full on first mention, then "Harbor Lane". Never "HLC".
• The logo is the rope-knot mark plus the wordmark. Keep clear space equal to the knot's height. Don't recolor it or put it on busy photos.

Colors
Name  ·  Hex  ·  Use
Harbor Navy  ·  #1F3A5F  ·  Primary. Bags, signage, headers
Rope Tan  ·  #C8A97E  ·  Accents, kraft bag labels
Sea Glass  ·  #A8D5C2  ·  Seasonal and limited releases only
Sail White  ·  #F7F4EE  ·  Backgrounds

Type
• Headlines: a slab serif, bold, all caps for bag names.
• Body: a clean humanist sans.

Voice
Warm, plainspoken, a little salty. We sound like a neighbour who knows a lot about coffee, not a sommelier. Short sentences. Be honest about costs and prices (see how we explained the Pricing Review). No "artisanal", "curated" or "elevated".

Sustainability claims
• Only claim what we can prove. Say "industrially compostable" and not "compostable" or "eco-friendly" on its own.
• When we switch to compostable packaging from Bayside Packaging, the bag must say where it can be composted.
• For Finca La Esperanza, publish the price paid per lb.

Photography
Natural light, real staff, real customers (with permission, per the Staff Handbook). The roaster in action is our best content (see Instagram Strategy).

notes.label: Instagram Strategy
notes.text:
Instagram is our main marketing channel. 6,200 followers as of late September 2026, and the goal is 8,000 by 31 December 2026.

Cadence
• 3 feed posts or reels per week (Mon, Wed, Sat) plus stories most days.
• Best time to post: 7–8am, when people are deciding where to get coffee.
• Boosting budget is $150/month, spent only on posts that are already doing well organically.

What works (from Q2–Q3 data)
1. Roasting reels. Beans dropping into the cooling tray get about 3× the reach of anything else. Film on Wednesday wholesale roasts (see Roasting Schedule).
2. Staff faces and latte art (with consent, per the Staff Handbook).
3. Honest posts. The pricing explainer post had our highest comment count ever (see Pricing Review).
4. Origin stories: farm photos from Finca La Esperanza. The February 2027 trip should give a month of content.

What doesn't
• Polished product shots on white backgrounds.
• Generic "happy Monday" posts.

Campaigns coming up
• Autumn menu teaser from 1 October, then launch day on 6 October (see Autumn Seasonal Menu).
• A Loyalty Program push: "double stamps week" in late October to bring back lapsed members.
• A holiday gift Subscription Service campaign from mid-November.

Tone & visuals
Follow the Brand Guidelines: natural light, Harbor Navy and Rope Tan, and no stock photos. Captions should sound like a person wrote them.

notes.label: Loyalty Program
notes.text:
A digital stamp card on the POS, launched 4 May 2026 to replace the paper punch cards. Set up by Priya Nair.

How it works
• Customers sign up at the till with a phone number or email.
• Buy 9 drinks, get the 10th free. Any drink, any size.
• A free birthday drink if they add their birthday.
• Stamps expire after 6 months of inactivity.

Numbers (to 25 September 2026)
• 1,140 members, about 55 new sign-ups per week at the start and about 25/week now.
• 22% redemption rate: of members who reached 9 stamps, 22% have redeemed.
• Members visit 2.1× per week on average versus an estimated 1.3× for non-members.
• Cost: about $1,350/month in free drinks at retail value, which is roughly $420/month at cost. It's covered by the marketing line in the 2026 Budget.

Watch items
• After the price increase on 1 October (see Pricing Review), track member visit frequency weekly. A drop below 1.8×/week for 3 weeks means we should rethink.
• About 30% of members haven't visited in 45+ days. Plan a "double stamps week" win-back in late October (see Instagram Strategy).

Ideas under discussion
• Tiers ("Deckhand" / "Captain"). Captain members would get 10% off retail bags.
• Linking the program to the Subscription Service, for example a free drink with every subscription renewal.
• Using the email list for the Autumn Seasonal Menu launch.

notes.label: Espresso Machine Maintenance
notes.text:
Our two-group espresso machine does about 450 shots on a busy Saturday. Downtime costs roughly $900 per morning in lost sales, so maintenance is not optional.

Daily (closing barista)
• Backflush each group with detergent. Water-only flush at midday.
• Soak portafilters and baskets in cleaner overnight.
• Purge and wipe steam wands after every drink. Soak the wand tips at close.
• Empty and wipe the drip tray.

Weekly (Sunday close)
• Check group gaskets and shower screens. Replace screens if the water spray is uneven.
• Clean the grinder burrs with grinder cleaning tablets.
• Record water hardness from the filter test strip.

Quarterly (technician)
• Descale and full service by Coastline Espresso Service. Costs $340 per visit.
• Last service: 19 August 2026. Next one due mid-November, before the holiday rush.
• Water filter cartridge replaced every 6 months. Last replaced in August 2026.

Incident log
• July 2026: a group 2 gasket failed at 7:40am on a Saturday. We ran on one group until noon. Gaskets are now replaced every 6 months instead of waiting for them to fail. Spare gaskets are kept in the roastery drawer.
• Feb 2026: steam boiler pressure switch replaced ($210).

The Seaview Hotel runs one of our older machines on loan, and their contract includes quarterly servicing by us. This matters for the renewal. Training on these tasks is part of Level 2 in the Staff Handbook.

notes.label: Health Inspection 2026
notes.text:
County health inspection on 12 March 2026. Unannounced, around 10:30am on a Thursday. Priya Nair was on shift and walked the inspector through.

Result
96 / 100. Passed. Up from 93 in 2025.

Findings (−4 points)
1. Hand sink partially blocked by the mop bucket (−2). Corrected on the spot. The closing checklist now says to keep the mop bucket away from the sink.
2. No thermometer in the under-counter milk fridge (−1). A thermometer was bought the same day, and temperatures are now logged twice daily (see Opening and Closing Checklist).
3. One staff member without a current food handler card (−1). Completed within the week. The Staff Handbook now requires it within 30 days of starting.

Positives noted
• Good separation of roastery and café areas.
• Pastry storage and labelling from Driftwood Bakery were fine.
• Cleaning logs for the espresso machine were up to date.

Follow-up
• Next routine inspection expected around March 2027.
• The inspector mentioned the roastery may need a separate permit if we start selling roasted coffee to more than 10 retail outlets. Worth checking before we expand Northgate Co-op-style accounts.

notes.label: Inventory Process
notes.text:
We do a full count every Sunday at close. Counts go into the shared inventory spreadsheet ("Stock 2026") before Monday 9am so orders can be placed.

Café stock (owner: Priya Nair)
Item  ·  Par level  ·  Supplier / notes
Whole milk  ·  24 gallons  ·  Dairy delivery Mon/Thu
Oat milk  ·  18 cartons (case of 6)  ·  Oat milk now 31% of milk drinks
12 oz hot cups  ·  2 sleeves of 1,000  ·  
Pastries  ·  Daily order  ·  Driftwood Bakery, ordered by 2pm the day before
Syrups  ·  2 bottles each  ·  Seasonal syrups for the Autumn Seasonal Menu

Roastery stock (owner: Daniel Reyes)
• Green coffee: keep at least 6 weeks of cover for every coffee in the Single Origin Lineup and Harbor Dark components. Reorder from the importer when cover falls below 8 weeks, because lead time is 3–4 weeks.
• Retail bags and labels from Bayside Packaging: reorder at 2,000 bags, since lead time is 6 weeks and the minimum order is 5,000.
• Degassing valves and mailer boxes for the Subscription Service.

Known issues
• Oat milk ran out twice in August. The par was raised from 12 to 18 cartons.
• Spreadsheet formulas broke when someone sorted the sheet. The columns are now locked.
• We would like POS-linked inventory eventually, but it's too expensive for the 2026 budget.

The weekly count takes about 45 minutes with two people.

notes.label: Opening and Closing Checklist
notes.text:
Laminated copy lives by the till. The shift lead initials each section on the daily sheet.

Opening (6:15am, doors at 7:00am)
1. Disarm alarm, lights, music (morning playlist).
2. Turn on espresso machine if it was powered down, and check boiler pressure.
3. Dial in espresso: Harbor Dark at 18 g in, 38 g out, 27–31 seconds. Taste before service.
4. Brew first batch of filter (current single origin).
5. Receive pastry delivery from Driftwood Bakery (6:30am) and check against the order.
6. Record fridge temperatures on the log sheet. Must be ≤ 41°F. This is required since the Health Inspection 2026.
7. Float the till with $200.
8. Wipe tables and put out the A-frame sign.

Closing (doors lock 4:00pm weekdays, 3:00pm Sundays)
1. Backflush and clean the machine per Espresso Machine Maintenance.
2. Clean the grinders, empty the hoppers of single origin (Harbor Dark can stay).
3. Mop the floor. Keep the mop bucket away from the hand sink.
4. Record fridge temperatures again.
5. Cash-up and count the till. Drop the safe bag. Variances over $5 go in the log.
6. Take out the trash and recycling. Coffee grounds go in the compost bin for the community garden.
7. Sunday only: full stock count per the Inventory Process.
8. Set alarm and lock both doors.

notes.label: Roasting Schedule
notes.text:
Roasting happens Monday, Wednesday and Friday on the 15 kg drum roaster. We average 22 batches a week (about 290 kg roasted). Daniel Reyes owns the schedule and posts it every Friday afternoon.

Weekly rhythm
• Monday: café stock, mostly Harbor Dark for espresso plus whichever single origin is on filter. Espresso rests 48 hours before use (degassing), so Monday roasts go on the bar from Wednesday.
• Wednesday: wholesale orders for Thursday packing and Friday delivery. Seaview Hotel alone is about 4 batches.
• Friday: online orders and the Subscription Service (packed Friday afternoon, shipped Monday morning), plus Northgate Co-op retail bags.

Rules of thumb
• Batch size is 12 kg green for Harbor Dark and 10 kg for single origins (lighter roasts need more airflow).
• Roast loss is 15–17% for Harbor Dark and 13–14% for light single origins.
• The first batch of the day is always a warm-up batch of Harbor Dark.
• Log every batch (charge temp, first crack time, development %, drop temp) in the roast log.

Capacity
The roaster could do about 40 batches a week, so we are at roughly 55% of capacity. Holiday season (Nov–Dec) pushes us to about 30 batches, and we add a Tuesday session.

Related: Inventory Process, Single Origin Lineup, Q4 priorities

notes.label: Staff Handbook
notes.text:
Summary of the handbook every new starter signs. Full PDF is in the shared drive.

Pay & tips
• Starting barista pay is $17.50/hour, rising to $18.75 after passing Level 2 certification.
• Tips are pooled weekly and split by hours worked. Card tips are paid out with payroll every other Friday.
• Roastery staff are paid $21/hour and are not in the café tip pool.

Time off & scheduling
• Request time off at least 2 weeks in advance through the rota app. Priya approves café requests and Daniel approves roastery ones.
• Shift swaps are fine if the manager on duty is told in the group chat.
• Late arrival more than 3 times in a month means a conversation with Priya Nair.

Training
• New baristas shadow 3 shifts before working the bar alone.
• Level 1: espresso dial-in, milk steaming, Opening and Closing Checklist.
• Level 2: latte art, Espresso Machine Maintenance (daily and weekly tasks), cash-up.
• Level 3 (optional): cupping with Daniel Reyes and roastery basics.

Perks & policies
• Free drinks on shift. One free 12 oz bag of coffee per month.
• 30% staff discount on retail bags and merchandise.
• Food safety: everyone completes the online food handler course within 30 days. This came up at the Health Inspection 2026.
• Social media: staff may post about the café, but follow the Brand Guidelines tone and never post customer faces without permission.

notes.label: Harbor Dark
notes.text:
Our house blend and bestseller. It's the espresso in every café milk drink, and it accounts for 38% of all roasted volume.

Components
• 60% Colombia, Finca La Esperanza: body, sweetness, red fruit.
• 40% Brazil, Cerrado Mineiro (via Pacific Green Importers): chocolate, nuttiness, low acidity.
• Recipe changed in 2024. It used to be 50/30/20 with a Sumatra component, which we dropped for consistency.

Roast profile
• Medium-dark. Drop at 224°C, development time ratio about 22%, total time 12:30–13:00.
• 12 kg green batches, with 15–17% roast loss (see Roasting Schedule).
• Rest 48 hours minimum before espresso use.

Tasting notes
Dark chocolate, toasted almond, molasses, with a clean finish.

Espresso recipe (café)
18 g in → 38 g out, 27–31 seconds, 93.5°C. Dialed in at every opening (see Opening and Closing Checklist).

Where it goes
• Café espresso and retail bags ($19.50 from 1 October, see Pricing Review).
• Almost every wholesale account: Seaview Hotel, Driftwood Bakery and Northgate Co-op.
• The default coffee in the Subscription Service "Harbor Dark only" plan.

Ideas
The "Seaview Signature" custom blend would be a Harbor Dark variant, probably 50% Colombia, 30% Brazil and 20% Ethiopia for a brighter cup.

notes.label: Single Origin Lineup
notes.text:
We offer three single origins at any time. They're on filter in the café, sold in retail bags ($22.50 from 1 October) and in the "Roaster's Choice" Subscription Service plan. The lineup rotates roughly every quarter.

Current lineup (autumn 2026)
Coffee  ·  Process  ·  Notes  ·  Cup score
Colombia, Finca La Esperanza  ·  Washed  ·  Red apple, panela, milk chocolate  ·  85.75
Ethiopia, Guji (Hambela)  ·  Natural  ·  Blueberry, jasmine, cocoa nib  ·  87.0
Guatemala, Huehuetenango  ·  Washed  ·  Caramel, orange, almond  ·  85.25

The Guatemala is also the base for the cold brew tonic on the Autumn Seasonal Menu.

Roasting
• Light to medium roasts in 10 kg batches with 13–14% roast loss. Daniel Reyes does all single-origin batches himself (see Roasting Schedule).
• Filter recipe: 22 g to 360 g water, 3:30 brew time.

Performance
• Single origins are about 18% of retail bag sales, but they have a higher margin than Harbor Dark at the new prices.
• The Ethiopia natural sells out fastest. Consider buying 50% more of it next year.

Next rotation (January 2027)
• Swap Guatemala for a Kenya (AA, washed) if samples cup at 86+. Samples were requested in September under Green Coffee Sourcing.
• Add the experimental honey process lot from Finca La Esperanza as a limited release when it arrives (probably spring 2027).

notes.label: Subscription Service
notes.text:
Coffee subscriptions sold through our online store. Launched in 2021 and part of the online & subscriptions stream in the 2026 Budget ($120k target).

Plans
Plan  ·  Frequency  ·  Price (current)  ·  Share of subscribers
Harbor Dark only (12 oz)  ·  Every 2 weeks  ·  $20.00 + shipping  ·  46%
Roaster's Choice (12 oz single origin)  ·  Every 2 weeks  ·  $23.00 + shipping  ·  31%
Monthly duo (2 × 12 oz)  ·  Monthly  ·  $39.00 + shipping  ·  23%

Numbers (September 2026)
• 312 active subscribers, down from 341 in March.
• Churn is 6.8% per month. The target is under 5%. The top cancellation reasons are "too much coffee" (38%), "price/shipping" (29%) and "moving/other" (33%).
• Average shipping cost to us has risen from $6.10 to $7.40 per parcel since January.

Operations
• Roasted on Friday, packed Friday afternoon and shipped Monday morning (see Roasting Schedule).
• Mailer boxes from Bayside Packaging at $1.12 each.
• Beans for the Roaster's Choice plan come from the Single Origin Lineup.

Changes planned
1. Pause instead of cancel: add a "skip a delivery" and "pause for a month" button. This targets the "too much coffee" churn.
2. Price change: existing subscribers get +$1.00 per shipment from 1 January 2027, and new subscribers pay the new price now (see Pricing Review).
3. Free shipping on the monthly duo plan to push people toward larger, less frequent shipments.
4. Holiday gift subscriptions (3 or 6 months) promoted through the Instagram Strategy from mid-November.
5. Maybe link to the Loyalty Program: subscribers get a free café drink each month.

notes.label: Bayside Packaging
notes.text:
Supplier for retail coffee bags, labels and mailer boxes since 2021. Our contact is Renee in customer accounts.

Current products & prices (quote dated June 2026)
Item  ·  Price  ·  MOQ  ·  Lead time
12 oz kraft valve bag (current)  ·  $0.62 each  ·  5,000  ·  6 weeks
12 oz compostable valve bag  ·  $0.91 each  ·  5,000  ·  8 weeks
4 oz sample bag  ·  $0.34 each  ·  2,000  ·  4 weeks
Printed labels (roll of 1,000)  ·  $78  ·  5 rolls  ·  2 weeks
Subscription mailer box  ·  $1.12 each  ·  1,000  ·  5 weeks

Notes
• Switching everything to compostable adds about $0.29/bag. At ~1,100 retail bags a month, that's about $320/month or $3,800/year.
• Northgate Co-op wants compostable packaging on their shelf by January 2027. To make that date we need to order by early November because of the 8-week lead time.
• The compostable bags are certified for industrial composting, not home composting. The wording on the bag has to be careful (see Brand Guidelines).
• The 4 oz sample bags could be used for Tom Whitaker's prospecting kits. Minimum order is 2,000, which is about a year's supply.
• Reorder triggers live in the Inventory Process.
• Net-30 terms. Always paid on time, and we got a 2% early-payment discount twice in 2025.

notes.label: Finca La Esperanza
notes.text:
Family farm in Pitalito, Huila, Colombia, run by Luis Cárdenas and his daughter Valentina. 14 hectares at 1,650–1,800 m. Castillo and Caturra varieties, washed process.

Relationship
• Third harvest buying directly (2024, 2025, 2026). We were introduced by an importer in 2023 and then moved to direct trade.
• 2026 contract: 60 bags (70 kg each), 4,200 kg total, at $4.60/lb FOB. Up from $4.10/lb in 2025.
• Payment terms: 40% on signing (paid in August 2026, $17,040), with the balance ($25,550) on arrival in November.
• Shipping and import are handled through Pacific Green Importers for a flat fee of $0.38/lb.

Quality
• Cupping scores: 85.5 (2024), 86.0 (2025), 85.75 (2026 pre-shipment sample).
• Tasting notes: red apple, panela, milk chocolate.
• It's the backbone of Harbor Dark (60% of the blend) and is sold on its own as part of the Single Origin Lineup.

Plans
• Origin trip in February 2027 during the harvest. Maya Okafor and possibly Daniel Reyes would go. Budget about $4,800 for flights and a week on the ground, not yet in the 2026 Budget (it's a 2027 cost).
• Luis wants to try a honey process lot. We committed to buying 5 bags of it as an experiment.
• Use the trip for Instagram Strategy content (farm story reels).

See Green Coffee Sourcing for how this fits the overall buying plan.

notes.label: Green Coffee Sourcing
notes.text:
How we buy green (unroasted) coffee. Daniel Reyes evaluates, and Maya Okafor signs contracts.

Principles
• Only buy lots that cup at 84+ on our Thursday cupping table.
• Prefer long-term relationships over chasing auction lots. Our goal is 50% of volume through direct or relationship trade by 2027. We're at about 35% today.
• Pay at least 25% above the commodity "C" price for every lot, and publish what we paid for relationship coffees.

Where our coffee comes from (2026)
Origin  ·  Share of volume  ·  Route
Colombia, Huila  ·  ~35%  ·  Direct: Finca La Esperanza
Brazil, Cerrado Mineiro  ·  ~30%  ·  Importer: Pacific Green Importers
Ethiopia, Guji  ·  ~15%  ·  Importer: Pacific Green Importers
Guatemala, Huehuetenango  ·  ~12%  ·  Importer (spot)
Other / limited  ·  ~8%  ·  Sample lots

Costs
• The average landed cost of green coffee is up 18% year-on-year ($4.05/lb in 2025 → $4.78/lb in 2026). This is the main driver behind the Pricing Review.
• Colombia is prepaid 40% at harvest contract signing. That's the $17,040 payment that squeezed August (see Cash Flow Q3 2026).

Process
1. Request samples (200 g) from importer offer sheets.
2. Sample roast on Tuesday afternoon, then cup on Thursday.
3. Approve, then Maya signs a forward contract, usually 3–6 months out.
4. Update the six-weeks-of-cover plan in the Inventory Process.

Components feed Harbor Dark and the Single Origin Lineup.

notes.label: Driftwood Bakery
notes.text:
Bakery two streets over on Cannery Row. It's both a wholesale customer (they serve our coffee) and a supplier (they bake our pastries). Owner: Sam Delgado.

As a customer
• About 18 lb/week of Harbor Dark, moving to the $12.25 tier on 1 October (see Wholesale Pricing).
• Account since 2020, one of our first wholesale customers.
• Problem: late payment. Average days-to-pay in 2026 is 41 days on net-30 terms. The worst was 67 days in May. They currently owe $1,480, with $610 more than 30 days overdue.

As a supplier
• Daily pastry delivery at 6:30am (croissants, morning buns, scones). About $1,900/month.
• Good quality, and customers love the morning buns. The pastries were fine at the Health Inspection 2026.

Options discussed
1. Offset: net their coffee invoice against our pastry invoice each month. Sam likes this idea.
2. Move them to net-15 or prepay.
3. Leave it as is. Not great given cash is tight (see Cash Flow Q3 2026).

Decision at the Team Meeting 2026-09-08: try the monthly offset from October. Tom Whitaker will set it up with the bookkeeper, and Maya will tell Sam directly because they're friends.

notes.label: Northgate Co-op
notes.text:
Member-owned grocery co-op on the north side of Port Alder, with about 4,000 members. They stock our 12 oz retail bags in the coffee aisle.

Account
• About 40 bags/week across 3 coffees: Harbor Dark, the Colombia single origin and a decaf.
• They buy at $11.20/bag from 1 October (see Wholesale Pricing) and sell at $14.99–$15.49.
• Buyer: Marcus Oyelaran. Orders every Wednesday for Friday delivery.
• Sales up 22% since we got an end-cap display in June 2026.

Asks from Northgate
• compostable packaging by January 2027. It's a co-op-wide policy for private and local brands. This needs the compostable bag from Bayside Packaging (+$0.29/bag) and an order by early November.
• Monthly in-store tasting demos. Tom Whitaker did two in the summer and each lifted that week's sales by about 30%.
• Roast date printed clearly on every bag (we already do this).

Considerations
• If compostable bags go co-op only, we'd run two bag SKUs. It's simpler to switch everything, and that fits the Brand Guidelines sustainability story.
• The county inspector flagged that a permit may be needed if retail outlets grow past 10 (see Health Inspection 2026).

notes.label: Seaview Hotel
notes.text:
Our largest wholesale account: a 120-room hotel on the Esplanade with a restaurant, lobby café and room service. Contact: Laura Kim, F&B Director.

Account facts
• About 55 lb/week: Harbor Dark for espresso, plus a decaf.
• Roughly $28k/year in revenue at the old prices, which is about 15% of wholesale revenue.
• On the >50 lb tier. They go from $9.90 to $10.50/lb on 1 October (see Wholesale Pricing).
• We loan them a two-group espresso machine and service it quarterly (see Espresso Machine Maintenance).

Contract renewal: due 15 November 2026
• The current 2-year contract expires 15 November.
• Laura has had an approach from a national roaster offering $9.20/lb plus free equipment.
• Our pitch: a custom "Seaview Signature" blend (+$0.75/lb custom fee waived for a 2-year term), a staff latte art training day, and faster service turnaround.
• Tom Whitaker and Maya Okafor are presenting the proposal on 21 October.
• Walk-away point: we won't go below $10.10/lb, because margin gets too thin with green costs up 18%.

Risks
• Losing Seaview would cut wholesale volume by about 16% and leave the roaster even further under capacity (see Roasting Schedule).
• It's on the list of Q4 priorities.

notes.label: Wholesale Pricing
notes.text:
Price list for café, restaurant and office accounts. New tiers take effect 1 October 2026, following the Pricing Review.

Tiers (per lb, roasted, 5 lb bags)
Weekly volume  ·  Old price  ·  New price (from 1 Oct)
Under 20 lb  ·  $11.50  ·  $12.25
20–50 lb  ·  $10.75  ·  $11.40
Over 50 lb  ·  $9.90  ·  $10.50

Single origins are +$1.50/lb on every tier. A custom blend is +$0.75/lb, with a 50 lb/week minimum.

Terms
• Net-30 for accounts older than 6 months. Prepay for the first 3 orders.
• Delivery Tuesday and Friday within 25 miles. Free over 20 lb, otherwise $12.
• Free barista training session (2 hours) at onboarding. Equipment loan available for accounts over 40 lb/week, with a servicing agreement.
• Late payment: 1.5% per month after 45 days. We have never actually enforced this, and that needs to change (see Driftwood Bakery).

Retail accounts
Grocery shelf accounts like Northgate Co-op buy 12 oz retail bags at $11.20 each (new price), and the retailer marks them up about 35%.

Margin check
At the new prices, gross margin on Harbor Dark wholesale is about 46% (it fell to 41% at the old prices once green costs rose). Target is 45%+.

Owner: Tom Whitaker. See also Seaview Hotel.
